# CLAUDE.md — Avoro Design Rules

> **Changes to this document must be followed by running the brand-guidelines-sync task in the tokens repo.**

This file is the rules layer that sits on top of `@avoro/brand-tokens`. Tokens give you the hex codes and font sizes. This document tells you **how to compose them**. Read both — neither is sufficient alone.

It is duplicated in two places on purpose:
- `AvoroGlobal/avoro-brand-tokens/CLAUDE.md` — for production engineering via Claude Code
- The Avoro Design System project (Claude design) — for wireframes, mockups, decks, marketing

When the two copies drift, the GitHub repo is the source of truth. Sync the design-system copy from it.

---

## 0. Shell rule — never draw chrome

You design surface content that mounts inside an existing shell (generic /s/[surfaceKey] host, role-based sidebar). NEVER draw navigation, sidebars, headers, or app chrome. Always load docs/design/platform-context.md first. Nav placement is a manifest decision made in the handoff interview, not a design decision.

(What the shell already provides, per archetype: the rail, tenant pill, account menu, and role-based nav — see the shell screenshots in `AvoroGlobal/keystone` `docs/design/shell-screens/`. Your canvas is the content area only.)

---

## 1. What Avoro is (one line)

Real estate's operating intelligence — one platform for real estate companies: agents, teams, and brokerages. Avoro sees the business, handles the work, and isolates what needs your judgment. Brokerage-agnostic. Confident operator, plainspoken, allergic to hype.

If a design choice would feel at home on a brokerage yard sign, it is wrong.

---

## 2. Tokens are the floor

Every color, font size, spacing value, radius, shadow, and motion curve must come from `@avoro/brand-tokens`. Never hardcode `#C8E83D` or `84px` in a component — import the token. If a value you need is not in the package, that is a token gap, not a license to invent. Raise it as a token addition first.

---

## 3. Color rules

### 3.1 The 60 / 30 / 10 rule
Roughly **60% Paper or Ink, 30% neutral support, 10% chartreuse.** Chartreuse never dominates a composition. A page that is mostly chartreuse is broken even if it's "on-brand."

### 3.2 The invert rule (load-bearing for accessibility)
Chartreuse `#C8E83D` **fails WCAG contrast on Paper**. Apply these rules without exception:

- **Slash glyph (`/`) on Paper backgrounds → render in Ink** (`#0E0E10`), not chartreuse.
- **Slash glyph on Ink backgrounds → render in chartreuse.**
- **Chartreuse-colored body or heading text on Paper → use `chartreuseDeep` (`#5C7A0A`)**, never the primary chartreuse.
- **Chartreuse as a fill** (CTA backgrounds, slash mark fills on dark surfaces) → primary chartreuse is fine.

In code: use the `surfaces.dark` / `surfaces.light` mappings in `@avoro/brand-tokens`, or the `[data-avoro-surface="dark|light"]` attribute selectors in `tokens.css`. They encode this rule for you.

### 3.3 Neutrals are warm
Paper is `#FAFAF7`, not `#FFFFFF`. Ink is `#0E0E10`, not pure black. Don't substitute pure white or pure black "to make it pop" — it breaks the warm neutral palette.

### 3.4 No gradients, ever
Solid fills only. This includes the slash itself, button fills, background blocks, hero panels, everything. If a design has a gradient anywhere, it is wrong.

### 3.5 Functional colors are editorial, not UI-loud
Success `#1F7A3D`, warning `#B8771A`, error `#A8242F`. Use sparingly and only for genuine state. No bright UI alert reds. No success greens that scream.

---

## 4. Type rules

### 4.1 Two families. No third.
**Geist Sans** for narrative prose (hero, headlines, body, UI).
**Geist Mono** for the wordmark, the slash, financial figures, code, eyebrows, footer fine print, mailto links, technical detail.
No Inter. No JetBrains Mono. No system font fallback as a substitute for Geist.

### 4.2 Four weights only
400 / 500 / 600 / 700. No Light. No ExtraBold. No Italic.

### 4.3 The wordmark is locked
`avoro/` — **lowercase always**, Geist Mono Medium (500), tracking `-0.02em`. Never `Avoro/`. Never `AVORO/`. Never any other weight.

### 4.4 Per-size tracking + leading are not optional
Each size step in the type scale has its own tracking and leading value. Use the size token's full triplet (size + tracking + leading). Tight hero leading and loose body leading are the system — overriding them flattens the typographic rhythm.

### 4.5 Eyebrows above headlines, never inline
Format: `01 / Color` or `THE PROBLEM` (Geist Mono, uppercase, letter-spacing `0.08em`, accent color). Eyebrows always sit above the headline on a separate line. Not inline. Not below.

### 4.6 Headings are sentence case
H1s are statements, not labels. "Seventeen logins is not an operating system." not "Login Consolidation".

---

## 5. Layout rules

### 5.1 Max widths
- Long-form content (essays, docs): **960px**.
- Marketing sections (hero, feature blocks): **1280px**.

### 5.2 Section spacing
- Marketing: **96px** between major sections.
- Product UI: **64px** between major sections.

### 5.3 Single-column on mobile. Two-column compare on tablet+.
No three-column layouts on tablet. No card grids that go to four columns below 1280px.

### 5.4 No sticky CTAs, no sticky banners
Only TOC sidebars may stick.

### 5.5 Full-bleed Ink is reserved
Use for hero sections, big quotes, and section dividers. Paper everywhere else. Don't alternate Ink and Paper section-by-section — it reads as "AI-generated landing page."

---

## 6. Components

### 6.1 Cards
On Paper: **1px border on Fog**, no shadow. Reserve shadow for elevation states (hover, focus, modal). Don't double up (border + shadow) on resting state.

### 6.2 Buttons
- Primary (chartreuse fill on Ink) → hover: `chartreuseBright`. Press: translate-y 1px, no scale.
- Primary (Ink fill on Paper) → hover: `inkSoft`. Press: translate-y 1px.
- No outline buttons with chartreuse stroke on Paper (contrast fails).

### 6.3 Status indicators
Pill chips, bordered tags. **Never "protection gradients."** Never glow.

### 6.4 Inputs
1.5px Fog border on Paper. Ink border on focus. No box-shadow focus rings — border color change carries the focus state.

### 6.5 Corner radii — pick one per element type
- `sm` (4px): chips, inline code
- `md` (8px): buttons, inputs, code blocks
- `lg` (12px): cards
- `xl` (20px): large containers, hero demos
- `pill` (999px): status badges, capsule CTAs

**No mixed-radius cards** (don't round only one corner). No fully square corners except inside the wordmark/slash itself.

---

## 7. Motion

### 7.1 Durations
- `120ms` for hover state changes.
- `200ms` for state changes (selection, expand, color shift).
- `320ms` for sheet/modal enter.

### 7.2 Easings
- `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` standard (most things).
- `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)` decelerate (entering).
- `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` accelerate (exiting).

### 7.3 What we never do
- No bounces. No spring physics.
- No long parallax.
- Nothing scales from 0.
- Default entry is **fade + 4px translate**. That's it.

---

## 8. Off-limits — the "never" list

These are deal-breakers. If a design has any of these, fix it before shipping, even if the design "looks better" with them.

### Visual
- Glassmorphism / `backdrop-filter: blur`.
- Gradients anywhere (including on the slash).
- Drop shadows that are gray, colored, or long.
- Inner shadows.
- Noise overlays, textures, repeating patterns.
- Opacity-based disabled states (use `color: smoke` on `bg: soft` instead).
- Bouncy / spring animations.
- "Hero scale-from-0" entrances.

### Iconography
- House, roof, door, key, gavel icons.
- Trees, lawns, suburban skylines, for-sale signs.
- "Family" pictograms, hand-holding, hearts.
- Any emoji, anywhere — product, marketing, docs.

### Imagery
- Stock photography of any kind until commissioned brand photography arrives.
- Staged living rooms, agent headshots in suits, hands shaking over property documents.

### Copy
- The word "realtor" or "REALTOR®" anywhere.
- "Home" when we mean "property" or "listing."
- "Family," "passion," "journey," "dream home," "empower," "revolutionize," "unlock," "ecosystem," "game-changer," "seamless," "next-generation," "world-class," "proud to announce."
- **"Splits" in any form — HARD BAN.** Avoro NEVER pays splits or moves commission money. Never depict Avoro paying, running, handling, or managing splits (or "payouts"). Use expense ratio / commission economics / production.
- Calendar-year language ("Year 1," "by 2027"). Use **Phase 1 / 2 / 3**.
- Exclamation points outside genuine product success states.
- Decorative em-dashes used for hype.

---

## 9. Voice rules

### 9.1 Pronoun (surface-locked)
- **"we"** for customer-facing copy (product UI, marketing site, recruiting, social, support).
- **"Avoro"** for third-party copy (investor updates, press, board materials, legal-adjacent).
- Never mix within a single asset.

### 9.2 Casing
- The wordmark is lowercase always: `avoro/`.
- All pillar slugs are lowercase, no spaces, forward slash: `avoro/agents`, `avoro/teams`, `avoro/brokerages`, `avoro/capital`, `avoro/intelligence`, `avoro/commerce`.
- Sentence case for headings. Mono accents (eyebrows, footers, status tags) use UPPERCASE with letter-spacing `0.04–0.08em`.

### 9.3 Sentence shape
- Short sentences carry weight. Cut the preamble. Start at the point.
- Name the number. GCI, expense ratio, cap rates, basis points — real numbers beat adjectives.
- Lead with the operator truth: "would a top-producing team leader nod at this?"

### 9.4 Preferred swaps
| Avoid | Prefer |
|---|---|
| solution, ecosystem | **platform** |
| professional, practitioner | **operator** |
| manage (your business) | **run** |
| compensate | **pay** |
| launch, deliver | **ship** |
| the ROI, the value prop | **the math** |
| operating system (as what Avoro is), rails | **operating intelligence** |
| payouts | *(banned — Avoro doesn't do payouts; name the actual work)* |
| just "teams" as the audience | **real estate companies — agents, teams, brokerages** |

### 9.5 Tone by surface
- **Marketing**: medium formality, medium-high energy. _"Profit is leaking while revenue rises. Avoro finds the leak."_
- **Product UI**: low formality, low energy, low technical depth. _"Done. Next move: the two listings going stale."_
- **Investor**: high formality, low energy, very high technical depth. _"Platform GCI under management grew 4.2× quarter-over-quarter. Gross margin held at 71%."_
- **Social**: low formality, high energy. _"Seventeen logins is not an operating system."_

### 9.6 The tagline
> "Real Estate's Operating Intelligence."

Updated 2026-08-06, replacing "The operating system for modern real estate teams." Matches avoroglobal.com. Use on the homepage hero, the deck cover, and the one-pager. "Operating system" appears in Avoro copy only as a foil ("Seventeen logins is not an operating system.") — never as what Avoro is.

---

## 10. Decision rubric — when in doubt

Before shipping a screen or component, walk this list:

1. **Tokens.** Is every value imported from `@avoro/brand-tokens`?
2. **60 / 30 / 10.** Is chartreuse coverage ≤ ~10%?
3. **Invert rule.** Where does chartreuse appear? On Ink → fine. On Paper as fill → fine. On Paper as type → must be `chartreuseDeep`.
4. **Type families.** Only Geist Sans + Geist Mono? No third typeface?
5. **Gradients / glassmorphism / bouncy motion.** None?
6. **Off-limits iconography / imagery / copy.** Clean?
7. **Voice.** Does it pass the "top-producing team leader nod" test?
8. **Pronoun.** "we" or "Avoro," consistent with surface?
9. **State.** Loading / empty / error states handled, all using the same rules?

If you can answer yes to all nine, the design is on-brand. If you can't, fix what's wrong before calling it done.
